required_tuples.rationale: A pinned existing install boots repeatedly with byte-identical schema SQL and sqlite_master identities plus unchanged fixture row and file values, so repeat boot preserves schema and selected records.
Fresh init creates the current pinned schema and zero users, POST /init creates one active root whose id/type survive upstream reopen and login, proving fresh-root identity is preserved.
Deleting the server-settings row and rebooting recreates exactly the pinned defaults with a generated token secret and fresh timestamps while root login still works.
Boot on an unreadable database file exits with status 1 and leaves the file byte-identical with no -wal/-shm/-journal sidecars, proving refusal without mutation and rollback-journal mode.
Created bookmark and progress rows, their JSON storage and read-back values (including null finishedAt) are all unchanged after upstream reopens the install, and the unauthenticated read is 401.
A local session is stored with all pinned column values and appears in listening history; an older session does not overwrite newer progress, and both survive upstream reopen unchanged.
PATCH media title updates the book row, the trigger-maintained item title and metadata.json (with no collateral changes), and all three remain readable after pinned upstream reopens.
The first progress and bookmark writes persist pinned UTC date spellings, TEXT JSON columns, JSON-millisecond values and integer booleans, and read back as JSON milliseconds.
Repeating a finish write keeps finishedAt and createdAt pinned while currentTime/duration change and updatedAt moves strictly forward, with the pinned finishedAt read back as JSON milliseconds.

bookAuthors rows persist in creation order, trigger-maintained authorNames columns follow that order, an unlinked author row is kept while another book links it, and series link sequence/removal persist.
An unknown-but-valid JSON field in a users TEXT column survives boot and is still present after a later write rewrites that same column, with updatedAt moving forward.
Invalid bookmark payloads answer 400 and unknown items answer 404 across progress/bookmark/series routes while every column of the users row stays byte-identical.
An aborted bookmark UPDATE exits the server with status 1, leaves the users row untouched, and after removing the trigger and reopening upstream the original bookmarks load unchanged.
The first PATCH merges only the supplied key into the stored document, keeps other defaults and createdAt, moves updatedAt strictly forward, and never surfaces tokenSecret.
An identical repeat patch and a patch of only non-patchable/unknown keys answer 200 and leave the settings row, including updatedAt, completely unchanged.
Sustained concurrent disjoint patches leave both changes in the stored document and the surfaced /api/authorize settings, proving a read-modify-write cannot lose the independent update.
Three sequential disjoint settings writes merge into one stored and surfaced document, and both row/timestamp and served values survive upstream reopen unchanged.
An invalid allowedOrigins update is rejected 400 and a non-admin patch is rejected 403 before any write, leaving stored and surfaced settings byte-identical.
With ALLOW_IFRAME=1 a patch disabling iframe is rejected 400 with no write, while the in-memory override surfaces allowIframe=true without persisting it.

An aborted settings upsert exits the server with status 1 and leaves the document/timestamp intact; after removing the trigger and reopening upstream the original settings load and further writes succeed.

not_applicable.reason: confirmed: persisted writers only create, update and reject values with no force/override operation (server/models/MediaProgress.js:190-245, server/models/Book.js:440-487, server/objects/settings/ServerSettings.js:365-381).
confirmed: production boot exposes no force action; Database.init(force=false) at server/Database.js:174-176 is documented test-only, dropping and recreating all tables.
confirmed: PATCH /api/settings filters the body to patchable keys and merges them (server/controllers/MiscController.js:152-163); there is no force or override mode.
